# jcli — full documentation

> jcli is a command-line tool for Jira workflow management, written in Go. It lets a
> developer pick the Jira issue they are working on without opening a browser, remembers
> that issue across shell sessions, and generates a consistent git branch name from the
> issue key and summary.

Site: https://jcli.tutunak.com/
Source: https://github.com/tutunak/jcli
License: MIT
Language: Go (requires Go 1.21 or later to build)
Platforms: Linux and macOS, amd64 and arm64

## What problem it solves

Working a Jira ticket normally means leaving the terminal: open Jira in a browser, find the
ticket, copy the key, switch back, and reconstruct what you were doing. jcli removes that
round trip. You select an issue once, and the terminal remembers it — so `jcli issue branch`
can hand you a branch name, and `jcli issue current` can remind you what you picked.

It is deliberately small: three issue commands, three config commands, no CLI framework, no
daemon, no cache. It talks to the Jira REST API v3 over HTTPS with Basic Auth (email plus API
token), and writes only to the XDG config and state directories.

## Installation

With Go:

```bash
go install github.com/tutunak/jcli@latest
```

From source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tutunak/jcli.git
cd jcli
make build
mv jcli /usr/local/bin/
```

Prebuilt binaries for linux and darwin (amd64 and arm64) are published on the
releases page: https://github.com/tutunak/jcli/releases

## Configuration

jcli reads a YAML file at `~/.config/jcli/config.yaml` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/jcli/config.yaml`
when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set). The directory is created with mode 0700.

```yaml
jira:
  url: https://yourcompany.atlassian.net
  email: your.email@company.com
  api_token: your_api_token_here

defaults:
  project: PROJ
  status: In Progress
```

Set it up interactively:

```bash
jcli config credentials          # prompts for Jira URL, email and API token
jcli config project MYPROJ       # default project key
jcli config status "In Progress" # default status filter
```

A Jira API token is created at
https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens

### Environment variables

Each of these overrides the corresponding value from the config file at load time. Useful for
CI, for keeping the token out of a file on disk, or for pointing jcli at a second Jira
instance for one command.

| Variable         | Overrides          |
|------------------|--------------------|
| `JIRA_URL`       | `jira.url`         |
| `JIRA_EMAIL`     | `jira.email`       |
| `JIRA_API_TOKEN` | `jira.api_token`   |
| `JIRA_PROJECT`   | `defaults.project` |
| `JIRA_STATUS`    | `defaults.status`  |

`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `XDG_STATE_HOME` relocate the config and state directories.

### File locations

| File   | Location                         | Purpose                       |
|--------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Config | `~/.config/jcli/config.yaml`     | Jira credentials and defaults |
| State  | `~/.local/state/jcli/state.json` | Current issue tracking        |

## Commands

### `jcli issue select`

Interactive picker. Queries Jira for issues in the configured project, in the configured
status, assigned to the authenticated user, most recently updated first. The underlying JQL is:

```
project = <PROJECT> AND status = "<STATUS>" AND assignee = currentUser() ORDER BY updated DESC
```

Navigate with the arrow keys, choose with Enter. The selection is written to the state file, so
it survives closing the terminal.

```
$ jcli issue select
? Select an issue
> PROJ-123: Implement user authentication
  PROJ-124: Fix login redirect bug
  PROJ-125: Add password reset flow
Selected: PROJ-123 - Implement user authentication
```

If the project or status matches nothing, jcli says so and exits without changing the
selection. If credentials are missing it points you at `jcli config credentials`.

### `jcli issue select <KEY>`

Select a specific issue directly, skipping the picker. The issue is fetched by key, so it does
not have to be assigned to you or match the configured status.

```
$ jcli issue select PROJ-456
Selected: PROJ-456 - Add rate limiting to the API
```

### `jcli issue current`

Print the issue currently selected, with the time it was selected.

```
$ jcli issue current
Current issue: PROJ-123
Summary: Implement user authentication
Selected at: 2024-01-15 10:30:00
```

With nothing selected it prints `No issue currently selected.` and exits successfully.

### `jcli issue branch`

Print a git branch name for the current issue, and nothing else — so it composes with git:

```bash
git checkout -b $(jcli issue branch)
```

```
$ jcli issue branch
PROJ-123-implement-user-authentication-847291
```

The format is `<ISSUE-KEY>-<normalized-summary>-<random>`, where:

- the issue key keeps its original case (so it stays uppercase, and stays greppable);
- the summary is lowercased, with accented Latin characters folded to ASCII (`é` to `e`, `ñ` to `n`, and so on);
- every remaining run of non-alphanumeric characters becomes a single hyphen, and leading and trailing hyphens are trimmed;
- the summary is truncated at 50 characters, backing up to the last hyphen when that avoids cutting a word in half;
- a random number from 0 to 999999 is appended, so re-running the command never collides with a branch you already made.

With nothing selected it prints a hint and exits non-zero, which keeps
`git checkout -b $(jcli issue branch)` from creating a garbage branch.

### `jcli config credentials`

Prompt for Jira URL, email and API token, then write them to the config file.

### `jcli config project <KEY>`

Set the default project key used by the interactive picker.

### `jcli config status <NAME>`

Set the default status filter. Defaults to `In Progress`. Quote values containing spaces.

### `jcli version`

Print the version. `--version` and `-v` are accepted too.

### `jcli help`

Print usage. `--help` and `-h` are accepted too. Running `jcli` with no arguments does the same.

## Typical session

```bash
# One-time setup
jcli config credentials
jcli config project MYPROJ

# Daily workflow
jcli issue select                    # pick an issue to work on
jcli issue current                   # verify the selection
git checkout -b $(jcli issue branch) # create the feature branch

# Or select and branch in one go
jcli issue select MYPROJ-456
git checkout -b $(jcli issue branch)
```

## Architecture notes

For anyone reading or contributing to the source:

- `cmd/` — command handlers. `root.go` routes on `os.Args[1]` with a switch; there is no CLI framework.
- `internal/jira/` — Jira REST API v3 client. `Client` is an interface so tests can use `MockClient`; `HTTPClient` makes the real calls with Basic Auth. Issue descriptions are `json.RawMessage` because Jira v3 returns ADF (Atlassian Document Format), not a string.
- `internal/config/` — YAML config loading, env overrides and saving.
- `internal/state/` — JSON state file holding the selected issue.
- `internal/branch/` — branch name generation and summary normalization.
- `internal/tui/` — the interactive selector, built on `github.com/charmbracelet/huh`.

Build with `make build`, test with `make test` (race detector and coverage), lint with
`make lint` (golangci-lint), and run the integration tests — which need real Jira
credentials — with `make test-integration`.
